question: Which treaty led to the surrender of nearly half of the territory of Mysore State to the East India Company?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seringapatam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790 – 1792):

 
 
• Tipu Sultan declared war on Travancore in 1789. Travancore was a friendly state of the British.
 
• In 1790, the Governor-General of Bengal, Lord Cornwallis declared war on Tipu Sultan.
 
• Tipu was defeated in the first phase of the war and his forces had to retreat.
 
• Later the English advanced towards Tipu’s capital of Seringapatam and Tipu had to bargain for peace.
 
 
 
• Result of the war:
 
 
• The war ended with the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792.
 
• As per the treaty, Tipu had to cede half of his kingdom to the English including the areas of Malabar, Dindigul, Coorg, and Baramahal.
 
• He also had to pay Rs.3 Crore as war indemnity to the British.
 
• Tipu also had to surrender two of his sons as surety to the British till he paid his due.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Treaty of Madras - First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69) 
 
• Treaty of Mangalore - Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-84) 
 
• Treaty of Salbai - First Anglo-Maratha war (1766–1769) 
 
• Treaty of Yandaboo - First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-1826)
 
• **Dindigul **is the first region to come under English rule in the Madurai District.
